notes: Supplemental written practice cards; existing MP3 narration is unchanged. Suggested scores are practice goals. Physical results are recorded by the student.

newTopics.title: A repeatable pre-shot routine
newTopics.summary: Make planning and delivery a repeatable physical routine.
newTopics.text: While standing, choose pocket, route, and finish. Approach along the aim line, form a comfortable stance and bridge, rehearse smoothly, pause as needed, and deliver. Stand up and restart if the plan changes. Use the straight-shot layout. Have a partner observe or record video, then review consistency of the routine rather than copying a prescribed body shape.

newTopics.title: Comfortable stance and cue clearance
newTopics.summary: Build comfortable balance and cue clearance while maintaining the chosen line.
newTopics.text: Plan while standing. Approach the shot, place your feet comfortably, and check that your body stays steady and the cue can move freely. Rise and realign if needed. Recreate the straight shot and observe from side/front video or with a coach. Adapt stance to your body; no single foot position is required.

newTopics.title: A stable bridge
newTopics.summary: Support a repeatable cue line with a stable bridge.
newTopics.text: Form a comfortable open or closed bridge on clear cloth. Rehearse slowly and check the hand remains still while the cue moves freely. Keep the bridge distance comfortable and consistent. Practice at the physical table with a coach, partner, or video. The on-screen cue does not model hand support or bridge stability.

newTopics.title: Relaxed grip and straight delivery
newTopics.summary: Deliver the cue through the intended tip contact with a relaxed grip.
newTopics.text: Choose center contact on an easy straight shot. Rehearse smoothly without squeezing or steering, then deliver through the ball while keeping the bridge stable. Use the straight-shot diagram and a striped practice ball if available to inspect unintended spin. Ask a coach to review persistent delivery errors.

newTopics.title: Reach, rail bridges, and cue access
newTopics.summary: Include physical cue access and reach when judging whether a route is practical.
newTopics.text: Compare a clear-cloth cue-ball start with a rail-adjacent start. Identify bridge support, cue clearance, reach, and elevation before choosing the stroke. Inspect the actual cue approach and use a mechanical bridge when needed. Do not stretch into an unstable stroke; compare a simpler accessible route.

aiming-line-quick.title: Aiming line
aiming-line-quick.purpose: Connect the chosen pocket, object-ball contact, and cue-ball approach.
aiming-line-quick.instruction: Name the pocket. Observe the ghost-ball center and contact line. Execute Shot, reset, then change only aim. Compare a full hit with a small cut.
aiming-line-quick.success: For each of five attempts, record the intended pocket and whether the object ball entered it. Separate an aim miss from a positional miss.
aiming-line-quick.transfer: Place the ball centers using the setup sheet. Visualize the ghost-ball center while standing, align the cue, and deliver the shot. Use five physical attempts; the software cannot measure your alignment or stroke.
aiming-line-quick.progression: Increase cue-ball distance or cut angle, one at a time, after a repeatable baseline.

tangent-line-quick.title: Tangent line
tangent-line-quick.purpose: Predict the initial cue-ball exit for a cut struck with stun at impact.
tangent-line-quick.instruction: Keep sidespin at zero. Compare the tangent reference with the initial path after collision. Adjust tip height or speed to approach stun; then compare follow and draw.
tangent-line-quick.success: Predict the initial exit side on three cuts, then record the pot and whether the initial route follows your tangent reference. Do not grade the entire follow/draw curve as a straight tangent.
tangent-line-quick.transfer: Use the cut layout and identify a rail crossing along the tangent. Test five attempts; watch the initial exit separately from the eventual stopping point.
tangent-line-quick.progression: Change cut angle, then compare how follow/draw move the route away from the reference.

diamond-grid-quick.title: Diamond references
diamond-grid-quick.purpose: Send the object ball through a planned cushion contact toward a pocket.
diamond-grid-quick.instruction: Use the bank reference as a starting estimate. Keep spin fixed, mark the first rail reference, and compare the object-ball rebound with the intended pocket route.
diamond-grid-quick.success: Record rail reference and bank made/missed over five attempts. Note whether the rebound runs short or long.
diamond-grid-quick.transfer: Copy the ball centers and identify the same rail point using diamonds. Start without added sidespin and adjust aim from observed rebounds.
diamond-grid-quick.progression: Change object-ball distance or speed individually, retaining the same target pocket.

trajectory-lines-quick.success: The intended operation completes and you can state what changed. This is an interface check, not a scored pool drill.
trajectory-lines-quick.transfer: Use the linked skill lesson or saved setup for physical practice. This software operation has no independent physical-shot score.

table-markers-quick.instruction: Choose a target marker, position it, and name its size. Use the cue-ball center as the scoring point; compare the leave against the boundary.
table-markers-quick.success: Record inside/outside for five attempts and keep the same marker size throughout the set. Shape/rotation changes the objective, not ball physics.
table-markers-quick.transfer: Use flat cloth-safe references that do not obstruct balls. Recreate the target size and center from the setup sheet; keep the boundary definition consistent.
table-markers-quick.progression: Start generously and shrink only after repeatable success.

physics-calibration-overview-quick.title: Physics and calibration overview
physics-calibration-overview-quick.purpose: Compare repeatable table behavior without confusing stroke changes with table changes.
physics-calibration-overview-quick.instruction: Use the defaults first. Save the baseline, repeat a simple shot, and record the pattern of differences. Advanced experiments change only one relevant parameter, then restore it.
physics-calibration-overview-quick.success: Retain a baseline and at least five physical observations. Check any adjustment on a second shot; one matching result does not validate all physics.

physics-calibration-overview-quick.progression: Keep separate baseline and experimental settings; do not tune a table from one inconsistent stroke.

follow-control-quick.title: Follow
follow-control-quick.purpose: Control forward cue-ball travel after pocketing a straight shot.
follow-control-quick.instruction: Choose a finish beyond the collision point and away from a pocket. Hold aim and speed fixed; compare two small follow settings and watch the stopping distance.

follow-control-quick.transfer: Place a flat visual target beyond contact. Reproduce the layout and aim for the same finish; judge your stroke by travel rather than copying a slider percentage.
follow-control-quick.progression: Use a smaller zone only after consistent pocketing and position; then increase approach distance.

masse-shot-controls-quick.success: Record obstacle avoidance, legal target first-contact, and cue-ball finish separately. Compare with a kick on the same layout.
masse-shot-controls-quick.transfer: Study the route on screen first. Attempt elevated curve shots only where permitted and with competent technique instruction; use a kick for ordinary physical practice if appropriate.
masse-shot-controls-quick.progression: Prefer the route you can repeat with the largest clearance margin.

setups.title: Massé shot controls
setups.note: Blocked direct lane plus room for lateral curvature; compare with a cushion escape.

execute-shot-sequence-quick.title: Execute Shot one at a time
execute-shot-sequence-quick.purpose: Use Execute Shot one at a time correctly within the current lesson.
execute-shot-sequence-quick.instruction: Select Execute Shot to simulate the active shot. If you have planned Shot 2, the trainer advances to that next planned cue ball after the current shot. Inspect the position before selecting Execute Shot again.
execute-shot-sequence-quick.success: The intended operation completes and you can state what changed. This is an interface check, not a scored pool drill.
execute-shot-sequence-quick.transfer: Use the linked skill lesson or saved setup for physical practice. This software operation has no independent physical-shot score.
execute-shot-sequence-quick.progression: Return to a skill lesson and use the control only when it helps the objective.

shot-two-leapfrog-quick.title: Continue planning beyond two shots
shot-two-leapfrog-quick.purpose: Pocket the current ball while preserving a usable angle on the next ball.
shot-two-leapfrog-quick.instruction: Name the next ball and pocket first. Mark a cue-ball zone and explain the angle it preserves. Execute Shot, inspect the actual simulated leave, and compare one speed or tip adjustment.
shot-two-leapfrog-quick.success: Record the first pot, zone arrival, and whether the next pot remains available as three separate outcomes over five attempts.
shot-two-leapfrog-quick.transfer: Set both object balls from the diagram. Play the first shot, then play the second from where the cue ball actually stops; no repositioning between those two shots.
shot-two-leapfrog-quick.progression: Shrink the useful zone or add a third ball; do not count an attractive leave that is blocked.

setups.title: First shot and next-ball position

shot-value-entry-quick.instruction: Adjust shot speed, follow and draw, or left and right spin by moving the slider, tapping the minus or plus buttons, or selecting the number box and typing an exact value. Exact values make it easy to repeat a shot and compare results.

cue-ball-diagram-direct-tip-quick.title: Direct cue-tip contact
cue-ball-diagram-direct-tip-quick.purpose: Control forward cue-ball travel after pocketing a straight shot.
cue-ball-diagram-direct-tip-quick.instruction: Choose a finish beyond the collision point and away from a pocket. Hold aim and speed fixed; compare two small follow settings and watch the stopping distance.
cue-ball-diagram-direct-tip-quick.success: Name a target zone before shooting. Record pot and cue-ball center in the zone separately over five attempts.
cue-ball-diagram-direct-tip-quick.transfer: Place a flat visual target beyond contact. Reproduce the layout and aim for the same finish; judge your stroke by travel rather than copying a slider percentage.
cue-ball-diagram-direct-tip-quick.progression: Use a smaller zone only after consistent pocketing and position; then increase approach distance.

cue-ball-pocket-power-meters-quick.title: C and P power meters
cue-ball-pocket-power-meters-quick.purpose: Distinguish cue-ball-to-object-ball power from object-ball-to-pocket power.
cue-ball-pocket-power-meters-quick.instruction: Keep aim and spin fixed. Reduce speed until the C or P meter is below its reference, then increase gradually. Execute to check contact and pocket arrival.
cue-ball-pocket-power-meters-quick.success: Identify whether the cue ball reaches the target and whether the object ball reaches the pocket. Enough power is not proof of correct aim or a successful pot.
cue-ball-pocket-power-meters-quick.transfer: Use the same shot and find the gentlest repeatable physical stroke that pockets the ball with a useful leave. Record pot and position separately.
cue-ball-pocket-power-meters-quick.progression: Compare a longer approach while keeping the target/pocket fixed.

jump-masse-open-controls-quick.title: Opening 3D jump and massé controls
jump-masse-open-controls-quick.purpose: Evaluate height at the obstacle, then landing and the continuation after landing.
jump-masse-open-controls-quick.instruction: Enable 3D controls. Identify the blocker crossing, clearance, and landing before Execute Shot. Change elevation or speed individually; do not use peak height as the clearance test.
jump-masse-open-controls-quick.success: In the simulator, record blocker avoided, target contacted, and landing inside a chosen zone separately. Missing clearance data is not evidence of clearance.
jump-masse-open-controls-quick.transfer: For physical practice, first confirm the venue permits jumps and use a suitable jump cue and supervised technique. Copy ball positions; start with an easy separation and score clearance and landing separately.
jump-masse-open-controls-quick.progression: Compare a simpler kick first; reduce the landing zone only after consistent clearance.

jump-masse-elevation-technique-advanced.purpose: Evaluate height at the obstacle, then landing and the continuation after landing.

jump-masse-elevation-technique-advanced.success: In the simulator, record blocker avoided, target contacted, and landing inside a chosen zone separately. Missing clearance data is not evidence of clearance.

jump-masse-elevation-technique-advanced.progression: Compare a simpler kick first; reduce the landing zone only after consistent clearance.

contact-point-geometry-quick.title: Contact point
contact-point-geometry-quick.purpose: Connect the chosen pocket, object-ball contact, and cue-ball approach.
contact-point-geometry-quick.instruction: Name the pocket. Observe the ghost-ball center and contact line. Execute Shot, reset, then change only aim. Compare a full hit with a small cut.
contact-point-geometry-quick.success: For each of five attempts, record the intended pocket and whether the object ball entered it. Separate an aim miss from a positional miss.
contact-point-geometry-quick.transfer: Place the ball centers using the setup sheet. Visualize the ghost-ball center while standing, align the cue, and deliver the shot. Use five physical attempts; the software cannot measure your alignment or stroke.
contact-point-geometry-quick.progression: Increase cue-ball distance or cut angle, one at a time, after a repeatable baseline.

cut-angle-geometry-quick.purpose: Recognize how a thinner contact changes cut angle, overlap, and the required aiming line.
cut-angle-geometry-quick.instruction: Keep the object ball and pocket fixed. Move only the cue ball to compare three cut angles. Predict which hit has less overlap before checking Live Stats.
cut-angle-geometry-quick.success: Correctly predict the fuller/thinner contact on three comparisons, then record pocketing on five attempts at each angle.
cut-angle-geometry-quick.transfer: Use the same object-ball spot and pocket. Mark three cue-ball starts by diamond references; reset the balls after each attempt.

tangent-line-geometry-quick.title: The tangent line

tangent-line-geometry-quick.instruction: Keep sidespin at zero. Compare the tangent reference with the initial path after collision. Adjust tip height or speed to approach stun; then compare follow and draw.

tangent-line-geometry-quick.progression: Change cut angle, then compare how follow/draw move the route away from the reference.

thirty-degree-rule-quick.title: The thirty-degree rule
thirty-degree-rule-quick.purpose: Recognize natural rolling departures and distinguish them from stun.
thirty-degree-rule-quick.instruction: Use a moderate cut and little sidespin. Allow natural roll at contact. Compare the eventual rolling direction with the approximately 30-degree reference when shown, then restore and test stun.
thirty-degree-rule-quick.success: Explain which trial arrives rolling and which arrives in stun. Predict the departure side before three different cuts; the 30-degree reference is an approximation over its useful hit range.
thirty-degree-rule-quick.transfer: Recreate the cut and observe the cue-ball route from rolling and stun deliveries. Use the direction as a starting reference, then check it on your table.
thirty-degree-rule-quick.progression: Compare a fuller and a thinner hit to learn where the natural-angle approximation stops being useful.

bank-shot-geometry-quick.transfer: Copy the ball centers and identify the same rail point using diamonds. Start without added sidespin and adjust aim from observed rebounds.
bank-shot-geometry-quick.progression: Change object-ball distance or speed individually, retaining the same target pocket.

kick-shot-geometry-quick.transfer: Copy the blocker and target. Identify the cushion-nose contact by diamond reference; reset all balls after each escape.
kick-shot-geometry-quick.progression: Aim for four target contacts in five as a suggested practice goal, then change the starting diamond.

exercise-table-speed.transfer: Measure the cushion-nose playing dimensions. Match ball starts with the setup sheet and record travel/finish. Normal practice does not require changing friction or restitution.
exercise-table-speed.progression: Keep separate baseline and experimental settings; do not tune a table from one inconsistent stroke.

rolling-sliding-comparison-advanced.transfer: Reproduce the cut without changing equipment mid-set. Record the object-ball result and cue-ball leave separately; precise spin transfer needs closer observation than the final leave alone.

natural-roll-quick.title: Natural roll
natural-roll-quick.purpose: Recognize natural rolling departures and distinguish them from stun.
natural-roll-quick.instruction: Use a moderate cut and little sidespin. Allow natural roll at contact. Compare the eventual rolling direction with the approximately 30-degree reference when shown, then restore and test stun.
natural-roll-quick.success: Explain which trial arrives rolling and which arrives in stun. Predict the departure side before three different cuts; the 30-degree reference is an approximation over its useful hit range.
natural-roll-quick.transfer: Recreate the cut and observe the cue-ball route from rolling and stun deliveries. Use the direction as a starting reference, then check it on your table.
natural-roll-quick.progression: Compare a fuller and a thinner hit to learn where the natural-angle approximation stops being useful.

physics-shot-speed-quick.title: Shot speed and distance
physics-shot-speed-quick.purpose: Predict and control stopping distance without changing the aiming line.
physics-shot-speed-quick.instruction: Choose a clear path. Name a stopping band, then test low, medium, and higher speeds from the same start. Reset between attempts.
physics-shot-speed-quick.success: Record short, inside, or long for five physical attempts at a named band. In the simulator, predict the ordering of three stopping distances.
physics-shot-speed-quick.transfer: Use a cue-ball-only route and flat target band. Translate stroke strength by observed travel; simulator speed values are not a measurement of your physical stroke.
physics-shot-speed-quick.progression: Narrow the band or add a cushion only after establishing a consistent baseline.

physics-follow-quick.title: Follow through contact
physics-follow-quick.purpose: Control forward cue-ball travel after pocketing a straight shot.
physics-follow-quick.instruction: Choose a finish beyond the collision point and away from a pocket. Hold aim and speed fixed; compare two small follow settings and watch the stopping distance.
physics-follow-quick.success: Name a target zone before shooting. Record pot and cue-ball center in the zone separately over five attempts.
physics-follow-quick.transfer: Place a flat visual target beyond contact. Reproduce the layout and aim for the same finish; judge your stroke by travel rather than copying a slider percentage.
physics-follow-quick.progression: Use a smaller zone only after consistent pocketing and position; then increase approach distance.

setups.title: Follow through contact
setups.note: Approach distance and contact geometry selected for Follow through contact.

physics-draw-quick.title: Draw through contact
physics-draw-quick.purpose: Retain backspin through impact and control the distance the cue ball returns.
physics-draw-quick.instruction: Keep the shot straight and sidespin at zero. Choose a return zone. Compare draw at a fixed speed, reset, then compare speed at a fixed draw setting.
physics-draw-quick.success: Record the pot and whether the cue-ball center returns into the selected zone on five attempts; distinguish no draw, short draw, and excessive draw.
physics-draw-quick.transfer: Place a flat target on the approach side of the object ball. Use your own cue delivery to reproduce the finish, resetting both balls for each attempt.
physics-draw-quick.progression: Move the cue ball farther away while retaining the same return-zone objective.

setups.title: Draw through contact
setups.note: Approach distance and contact geometry selected for Draw through contact.

physics-stun-quick.title: Stop and stun
physics-stun-quick.purpose: Predict the initial cue-ball exit for a cut struck with stun at impact.
physics-stun-quick.instruction: Keep sidespin at zero. Compare the tangent reference with the initial path after collision. Adjust tip height or speed to approach stun; then compare follow and draw.
physics-stun-quick.success: Predict the initial exit side on three cuts, then record the pot and whether the initial route follows your tangent reference. Do not grade the entire follow/draw curve as a straight tangent.
physics-stun-quick.transfer: Use the cut layout and identify a rail crossing along the tangent. Test five attempts; watch the initial exit separately from the eventual stopping point.
physics-stun-quick.progression: Change cut angle, then compare how follow/draw move the route away from the reference.

setups.title: Stop and stun
setups.note: Approach distance and contact geometry selected for Stop and stun.

physics-english-quick.title: Side spin or English
physics-english-quick.purpose: Distinguish sidespin influence on the approach from its effect at a cushion.
physics-english-quick.instruction: Start with no sidespin, restore, then compare equal left and right settings. Keep speed and the starting aim fixed for the first comparison; inspect the incoming and outgoing paths separately.
physics-english-quick.success: Predict the change of rebound side before each comparison. On the physical table, record the rail arrival and finish for five shots at each setting.
physics-english-quick.transfer: Use the rail layout and the same cushion reference. Establish a no-English baseline before compensating aim for sidespin.
physics-english-quick.progression: Add a target zone; then compare a second speed without changing the layout.

cue-ball-squirt-quick.title: Cue ball deflection or squirt
cue-ball-squirt-quick.purpose: Recognize initial cue-ball deflection when using off-center contact.
cue-ball-squirt-quick.instruction: Keep the cue near level. Compare center, left, and right contact at the same aim and speed. Observe the initial cue-ball path before a cushion or collision; then test an aim correction.
cue-ball-squirt-quick.success: Predict the initial deflection side and identify the correction needed. Record contact accuracy for five physical trials, keeping the cue/shaft the same.
cue-ball-squirt-quick.transfer: Recreate a long approach. Observe initial departure separately from later curvature; use your own cue response rather than assuming the preset matches it exactly.
cue-ball-squirt-quick.progression: Compare distances before introducing elevation and swerve.

cue-ball-swerve-advanced.title: Swerve and cloth interaction
cue-ball-swerve-advanced.purpose: Separate initial deflection from later cloth-induced curvature.
cue-ball-swerve-advanced.instruction: Use a clear approach, small sidespin, and modest elevation. Compare the initial direction and later path at two speeds; change only one setting at a time.
cue-ball-swerve-advanced.success: Identify initial deflection versus later curvature in three comparisons. Record whether the target contact shifts left or right.
cue-ball-swerve-advanced.transfer: Use a permitted low-elevation setup with clear cue access. Observe the path from a consistent view or video; the simulator cannot diagnose delivery.

structured-practice-intro-quick.title: Introduction to structured practice
structured-practice-intro-quick.purpose: Use comparable results to decide what to practice next.
structured-practice-intro-quick.instruction: Choose one saved layout and fixed scoring conditions. Record attempts, pots, position, and legal contact where applicable; note one repeatable error and one adjustment.
structured-practice-intro-quick.success: Complete a baseline set and a later set under the same conditions. Report both, rather than only the best attempt; simulator repetition is not evidence of physical skill improvement.
structured-practice-intro-quick.transfer: Use five or ten physical attempts with the same layout, zone, and cue. Record the date and conditions, then begin the next session with that baseline.
structured-practice-intro-quick.progression: Increase one difficulty factor only after consistent results; suggested targets are practice goals, not certified ratings.

practice-aiming-quick.title: Learning to aim accurately
practice-aiming-quick.purpose: Connect the chosen pocket, object-ball contact, and cue-ball approach.
practice-aiming-quick.instruction: Name the pocket. Observe the ghost-ball center and contact line. Execute Shot, reset, then change only aim. Compare a full hit with a small cut.
practice-aiming-quick.success: For each of five attempts, record the intended pocket and whether the object ball entered it. Separate an aim miss from a positional miss.
practice-aiming-quick.transfer: Place the ball centers using the setup sheet. Visualize the ghost-ball center while standing, align the cue, and deliver the shot. Use five physical attempts; the software cannot measure your alignment or stroke.
practice-aiming-quick.progression: Increase cue-ball distance or cut angle, one at a time, after a repeatable baseline.

setups.title: Learning to aim accurately
setups.note: Approach distance and contact geometry selected for Learning to aim accurately.

practice-speed-control-quick.title: Developing speed control
practice-speed-control-quick.purpose: Predict and control stopping distance without changing the aiming line.
practice-speed-control-quick.instruction: Choose a clear path. Name a stopping band, then test low, medium, and higher speeds from the same start. Reset between attempts.
practice-speed-control-quick.success: Record short, inside, or long for five physical attempts at a named band. In the simulator, predict the ordering of three stopping distances.
practice-speed-control-quick.transfer: Use a cue-ball-only route and flat target band. Translate stroke strength by observed travel; simulator speed values are not a measurement of your physical stroke.
practice-speed-control-quick.progression: Narrow the band or add a cushion only after establishing a consistent baseline.

setups.title: Developing speed control
setups.note: Clear rolling lane and a named stopping target; no collision hides the travel comparison.

practice-stop-shot-quick.title: Understanding stop shots
practice-stop-shot-quick.purpose: Arrive at a straight full-ball collision without forward or backward roll.
practice-stop-shot-quick.instruction: Use a straight shot with no sidespin. Start slightly below center, keep aim fixed, and adjust one of tip height or speed. Observe the cue-ball center at impact and at rest.
practice-stop-shot-quick.success: Count five attempts: record the pot and a cue-ball finish within one ball diameter of its center at impact. Count a pot with unwanted roll as a position miss.
practice-stop-shot-quick.transfer: Use the setup sheet and choose the same stopping tolerance on the cloth. Record pot and stop separately; recreate the original ball centers after every attempt.
practice-stop-shot-quick.progression: Increase approach distance; regain the stop with speed and tip height rather than assuming center-tip contact always means stun.

setups.title: Understanding stop shots
setups.note: Approach distance and contact geometry selected for Understanding stop shots.

practice-follow-shot-quick.title: Practicing follow shots
practice-follow-shot-quick.purpose: Control forward cue-ball travel after pocketing a straight shot.
practice-follow-shot-quick.instruction: Choose a finish beyond the collision point and away from a pocket. Hold aim and speed fixed; compare two small follow settings and watch the stopping distance.
practice-follow-shot-quick.success: Name a target zone before shooting. Record pot and cue-ball center in the zone separately over five attempts.
practice-follow-shot-quick.transfer: Place a flat visual target beyond contact. Reproduce the layout and aim for the same finish; judge your stroke by travel rather than copying a slider percentage.
practice-follow-shot-quick.progression: Use a smaller zone only after consistent pocketing and position; then increase approach distance.

setups.title: Practicing follow shots
setups.note: Approach distance and contact geometry selected for Practicing follow shots.

practice-draw-shot-quick.title: Practicing draw shots
practice-draw-shot-quick.purpose: Retain backspin through impact and control the distance the cue ball returns.
practice-draw-shot-quick.instruction: Keep the shot straight and sidespin at zero. Choose a return zone. Compare draw at a fixed speed, reset, then compare speed at a fixed draw setting.
practice-draw-shot-quick.success: Record the pot and whether the cue-ball center returns into the selected zone on five attempts; distinguish no draw, short draw, and excessive draw.
practice-draw-shot-quick.transfer: Place a flat target on the approach side of the object ball. Use your own cue delivery to reproduce the finish, resetting both balls for each attempt.
practice-draw-shot-quick.progression: Move the cue ball farther away while retaining the same return-zone objective.

setups.title: Practicing draw shots
setups.note: Approach distance and contact geometry selected for Practicing draw shots.

practice-cut-angles-quick.title: Practicing cut angles
practice-cut-angles-quick.purpose: Recognize how a thinner contact changes cut angle, overlap, and the required aiming line.
practice-cut-angles-quick.instruction: Keep the object ball and pocket fixed. Move only the cue ball to compare three cut angles. Predict which hit has less overlap before checking Live Stats.
practice-cut-angles-quick.success: Correctly predict the fuller/thinner contact on three comparisons, then record pocketing on five attempts at each angle.
practice-cut-angles-quick.transfer: Use the same object-ball spot and pocket. Mark three cue-ball starts by diamond references; reset the balls after each attempt.
practice-cut-angles-quick.progression: Increase distance before adding English; keep the same scoring conditions.

setups.title: Practicing cut angles
setups.note: Approach distance and contact geometry selected for Practicing cut angles.

practice-tangent-line-quick.title: Practicing the tangent line
practice-tangent-line-quick.purpose: Predict the initial cue-ball exit for a cut struck with stun at impact.
practice-tangent-line-quick.instruction: Keep sidespin at zero. Compare the tangent reference with the initial path after collision. Adjust tip height or speed to approach stun; then compare follow and draw.
practice-tangent-line-quick.success: Predict the initial exit side on three cuts, then record the pot and whether the initial route follows your tangent reference. Do not grade the entire follow/draw curve as a straight tangent.
practice-tangent-line-quick.transfer: Use the cut layout and identify a rail crossing along the tangent. Test five attempts; watch the initial exit separately from the eventual stopping point.
practice-tangent-line-quick.progression: Change cut angle, then compare how follow/draw move the route away from the reference.

setups.title: Practicing the tangent line

practice-bank-shots-quick.title: Practicing bank shots
practice-bank-shots-quick.purpose: Send the object ball through a planned cushion contact toward a pocket.
practice-bank-shots-quick.instruction: Use the bank reference as a starting estimate. Keep spin fixed, mark the first rail reference, and compare the object-ball rebound with the intended pocket route.
practice-bank-shots-quick.success: Record rail reference and bank made/missed over five attempts. Note whether the rebound runs short or long.
practice-bank-shots-quick.transfer: Copy the ball centers and identify the same rail point using diamonds. Start without added sidespin and adjust aim from observed rebounds.
practice-bank-shots-quick.progression: Change object-ball distance or speed individually, retaining the same target pocket.

setups.title: Practicing bank shots
setups.note: Object-ball bank to a named corner, with a geometric first-rail reference; rebounds need observed adjustment. Prepared aim is adjusted from the geometric reference for the default simulator cushion response; recalibrate on your table.

practice-kick-shots-quick.title: Practicing kick shots
practice-kick-shots-quick.purpose: Reach the legal target through a cushion route when direct access is blocked.
practice-kick-shots-quick.instruction: Name the target and required rail sequence. Keep speed and sidespin consistent while adjusting only the first rail aim point. Check that the blocker is avoided.
practice-kick-shots-quick.success: Record target first-contact, scratch, and the game-required rail/pot condition on five attempts. A target touch is a contact score, not automatically a legal shot.
practice-kick-shots-quick.transfer: Copy the blocker and target. Identify the cushion-nose contact by diamond reference; reset all balls after each escape.
practice-kick-shots-quick.progression: Aim for four target contacts in five as a suggested practice goal, then change the starting diamond.

setups.title: Practicing kick shots

practice-english-quick.progression: Add a target zone; then compare a second speed without changing the layout.

first-session-welcome.title: 1. Welcome to Focused Practice
first-session-welcome.purpose: Connect the first pot with the cue-ball leave.
first-session-welcome.instruction: Name the intended pocket and next ball. Execute the prepared shot, then inspect whether the next shot is available.
first-session-welcome.success: Identify the potted ball and describe the leave; repeat once with a prediction before shooting.
first-session-welcome.transfer: Use the linked skill lesson or saved setup for physical practice. This software operation has no independent physical-shot score.
first-session-welcome.progression: Return to a skill lesson and use the control only when it helps the objective.

setups.title: Welcome to Focused Practice
setups.note: Get Started snapshot; physical setup sheet uses its starting positions, including the saved before-shot state in Undo practice.

first-session-aiming.title: 2. Set Up and Aim Precisely
first-session-aiming.purpose: Connect the chosen pocket, object-ball contact, and cue-ball approach.
first-session-aiming.instruction: Name the pocket. Observe the ghost-ball center and contact line. Execute Shot, reset, then change only aim. Compare a full hit with a small cut.
first-session-aiming.success: For each of five attempts, record the intended pocket and whether the object ball entered it. Separate an aim miss from a positional miss.
first-session-aiming.transfer: Place the ball centers using the setup sheet. Visualize the ghost-ball center while standing, align the cue, and deliver the shot. Use five physical attempts; the software cannot measure your alignment or stroke.
first-session-aiming.progression: Increase cue-ball distance or cut angle, one at a time, after a repeatable baseline.

setups.title: Set Up and Aim Precisely

first-session-speed.title: 3. Speed, Tip Contact, and English
first-session-speed.purpose: Retain backspin through impact and control the distance the cue ball returns.
first-session-speed.instruction: Keep the shot straight and sidespin at zero. Choose a return zone. Compare draw at a fixed speed, reset, then compare speed at a fixed draw setting.
first-session-speed.success: Record the pot and whether the cue-ball center returns into the selected zone on five attempts; distinguish no draw, short draw, and excessive draw.
first-session-speed.transfer: Place a flat target on the approach side of the object ball. Use your own cue delivery to reproduce the finish, resetting both balls for each attempt.
first-session-speed.progression: Move the cue ball farther away while retaining the same return-zone objective.

setups.title: Speed, Tip Contact, and English
setups.note: Get Started snapshot; physical setup sheet uses its starting positions, including the saved before-shot state in Undo practice.

first-session-execute.title: 4. Execute and Compare Variations
first-session-execute.purpose: Keep a repeatable starting arrangement so comparisons test one change.
first-session-execute.instruction: Save the layout, change one ball or setting, and recall the original. Check ball identities, positions, and intended pocket before comparing.
first-session-execute.success: Restore the same ball centers and reproduce the intended comparison. Distinguish ball-layout reset from a complete session/stroke-settings restoration.
first-session-execute.transfer: Use the coordinate sheet and a written record of the intended stroke. Mark or measure original ball centers and reset them between attempts.
first-session-execute.progression: Save baseline and variation under different names; keep physical results with the matching setup.

setups.title: Execute and Compare Variations
setups.note: Get Started snapshot; physical setup sheet uses its starting positions, including the saved before-shot state in Undo practice.

first-session-shot-two.title: 5. Plan and Execute Shot 2
first-session-shot-two.purpose: Pocket the current ball while preserving a usable angle on the next ball.
first-session-shot-two.instruction: Name the next ball and pocket first. Mark a cue-ball zone and explain the angle it preserves. Execute Shot, inspect the actual simulated leave, and compare one speed or tip adjustment.
first-session-shot-two.success: Record the first pot, zone arrival, and whether the next pot remains available as three separate outcomes over five attempts.
first-session-shot-two.transfer: Set both object balls from the diagram. Play the first shot, then play the second from where the cue ball actually stops; no repositioning between those two shots.
first-session-shot-two.progression: Shrink the useful zone or add a third ball; do not count an attractive leave that is blocked.

live-stats-squirt-quick.title: Predicted squirt
live-stats-squirt-quick.purpose: Recognize initial cue-ball deflection when using off-center contact.
live-stats-squirt-quick.instruction: Keep the cue near level. Compare center, left, and right contact at the same aim and speed. Observe the initial cue-ball path before a cushion or collision; then test an aim correction.
live-stats-squirt-quick.success: Predict the initial deflection side and identify the correction needed. Record contact accuracy for five physical trials, keeping the cue/shaft the same.
live-stats-squirt-quick.transfer: Recreate a long approach. Observe initial departure separately from later curvature; use your own cue response rather than assuming the preset matches it exactly.
live-stats-squirt-quick.progression: Compare distances before introducing elevation and swerve.

live-stats-jump-clearance-quick.title: Jump and clearance
live-stats-jump-clearance-quick.purpose: Evaluate height at the obstacle, then landing and the continuation after landing.
live-stats-jump-clearance-quick.instruction: Enable 3D controls. Identify the blocker crossing, clearance, and landing before Execute Shot. Change elevation or speed individually; do not use peak height as the clearance test.
live-stats-jump-clearance-quick.success: In the simulator, record blocker avoided, target contacted, and landing inside a chosen zone separately. Missing clearance data is not evidence of clearance.
live-stats-jump-clearance-quick.transfer: For physical practice, first confirm the venue permits jumps and use a suitable jump cue and supervised technique. Copy ball positions; start with an easy separation and score clearance and landing separately.
live-stats-jump-clearance-quick.progression: Compare a simpler kick first; reduce the landing zone only after consistent clearance.

live-stats-masse-quick.title: Curve and massé
live-stats-masse-quick.purpose: Compare a curved route around a blocker with a cushion alternative.
live-stats-masse-quick.instruction: Identify the lateral clearance needed. Change elevation, sidespin, or speed one at a time and inspect the whole curve, not just its endpoint.
live-stats-masse-quick.success: Record obstacle avoidance, legal target first-contact, and cue-ball finish separately. Compare with a kick on the same layout.
live-stats-masse-quick.transfer: Study the route on screen first. Attempt elevated curve shots only where permitted and with competent technique instruction; use a kick for ordinary physical practice if appropriate.
live-stats-masse-quick.progression: Prefer the route you can repeat with the largest clearance margin.

main-pick-and-play-full-racks.title: Pick and Play Full Racks
main-pick-and-play-full-racks.purpose: Use Pick and Play Full Racks correctly within the current lesson.
main-pick-and-play-full-racks.instruction: Pick and Play Full Racks prepares a complete game rack. Choose 3-Ball, 6-Ball, 7-Ball, 8-Ball, 9-Ball, 10-Ball, Ultimate 8 Ball, or Straight Pool from the menu, then press Start. Six Ball uses a small triangle. Seven Ball places the seven in the center of a hexagon. Straight Pool prepares fourteen balls with the front position open. Add a single ball if you want a separate break ball, then drag it and the cue ball to your preferred positions. Ultimate 8 Ball uses the fixed numbered arrangement and puts the eight ball exactly on the foot spot.

main-random-ball-count.transfer: Use the coordinate sheet and a written record of the intended stroke. Mark or measure original ball centers and reset them between attempts.
main-random-ball-count.progression: Save baseline and variation under different names; keep physical results with the matching setup.

practice-session-introduction.title: Practice pathway
practice-session-introduction.purpose: Use comparable results to decide what to practice next.
practice-session-introduction.instruction: Choose one saved layout and fixed scoring conditions. Record attempts, pots, position, and legal contact where applicable; note one repeatable error and one adjustment.
practice-session-introduction.success: Complete a baseline set and a later set under the same conditions. Report both, rather than only the best attempt; simulator repetition is not evidence of physical skill improvement.
practice-session-introduction.transfer: Use five or ten physical attempts with the same layout, zone, and cue. Record the date and conditions, then begin the next session with that baseline.
practice-session-introduction.progression: Increase one difficulty factor only after consistent results; suggested targets are practice goals, not certified ratings.

setups.title: Practice pathway
setups.note: Current pot plus a next-ball angle and a visible position zone.

existingPractice.Goal: Build accuracy, position, and recovery in a consistent order.
existingPractice.Measure: Record a baseline score before making the drill harder.
existingPractice.Trainer: Use Save Table File to keep or share the starting layout.

practice-speed-contact-baseline.title: Speed and contact baseline
practice-speed-contact-baseline.purpose: Arrive at a straight full-ball collision without forward or backward roll.
practice-speed-contact-baseline.instruction: Use a straight shot with no sidespin. Start slightly below center, keep aim fixed, and adjust one of tip height or speed. Observe the cue-ball center at impact and at rest.
practice-speed-contact-baseline.success: Count five attempts: record the pot and a cue-ball finish within one ball diameter of its center at impact. Count a pot with unwanted roll as a position miss.
practice-speed-contact-baseline.transfer: Use the setup sheet and choose the same stopping tolerance on the cloth. Record pot and stop separately; recreate the original ball centers after every attempt.
practice-speed-contact-baseline.progression: Increase approach distance; regain the stop with speed and tip height rather than assuming center-tip contact always means stun.

setups.title: Speed and contact baseline
setups.note: Approach distance and contact geometry selected for Speed and contact baseline.

existingPractice.Goal: Separate aim errors from cue ball control errors.
existingPractice.Setup: One object ball, one pocket, and a repeatable cue ball starting point.
existingPractice.Measure: Repeat each setting five times and identify the direction of the miss.
existingPractice.Trainer: Use cue tip contact, shot speed, tangent line, and Undo Last Shot.

practice-target-landing.title: Target landing precision
practice-target-landing.purpose: Pocket the current ball while preserving a usable angle on the next ball.
practice-target-landing.instruction: Name the next ball and pocket first. Mark a cue-ball zone and explain the angle it preserves. Execute Shot, inspect the actual simulated leave, and compare one speed or tip adjustment.
practice-target-landing.success: Use the existing target size chosen for this plan. Count only a pot plus cue-ball center inside the target. The narrated goal is 8 of 10; begin with a larger zone if needed.
practice-target-landing.transfer: Set both object balls from the diagram. Play the first shot, then play the second from where the cue ball actually stops; no repositioning between those two shots.
practice-target-landing.progression: Shrink the useful zone or add a third ball; do not count an attractive leave that is blocked.

setups.title: Target landing precision
setups.note: Current pot plus a next-ball angle and a visible position zone.

existingPractice.Goal: Control the cue ball stopping point after pocketing.
existingPractice.Setup: Use a three inch target, starting with an easier size if needed.
existingPractice.Measure: Pocket the ball and land the cue ball center inside the target on 8 of 10 attempts.
existingPractice.Trainer: Use a table marker for the landing zone; save the layout and use Undo to repeat it.

practice-rock-around-clock.title: Rock Around the Clock
practice-rock-around-clock.purpose: Choose a sequence that preserves angles, access, and manageable transitions.
practice-rock-around-clock.instruction: Compare two orders on the same layout. Explain the next-ball angle before each shot. Use Shot 2, execute one shot at a time, and revise from the resulting layout.
practice-rock-around-clock.success: Use the linked creator layout for its exact sequence. For the Trainer adaptation, record one completed rotation first, then work toward the narrated three consecutive rotations without disturbing another ball.
practice-rock-around-clock.transfer: Choose 8-ball-style open practice or lowest-ball-first rotation before starting. Play each run from the actual leaves; reset only at the end of a run.
practice-rock-around-clock.progression: Add a ball or a blocker while retaining a readable, explained pattern.

setups.title: Rock Around the Clock
setups.note: A distinct open pattern for comparing order, next angles, and route complexity.

existingPractice.Goal: Plan the next shot before shooting the current one.
existingPractice.Setup: Use the linked demonstration for the creator’s ball layout and sequence.
existingPractice.Measure: For this plan, complete 3 consecutive rotations without disturbing a secondary ball.
existingPractice.Trainer: Use Shot 2 to preview the next shot and Undo Last Shot to revisit a position error.

practice-one-rail-kick.title: One-rail kick reference
practice-one-rail-kick.purpose: Reach the legal target through a cushion route when direct access is blocked.
practice-one-rail-kick.instruction: Name the target and required rail sequence. Keep speed and sidespin consistent while adjusting only the first rail aim point. Check that the blocker is avoided.
practice-one-rail-kick.success: Record target first-contact, scratch, and the game-required rail/pot condition on five attempts. A target touch is a contact score, not automatically a legal shot.
practice-one-rail-kick.transfer: Copy the blocker and target. Identify the cushion-nose contact by diamond reference; reset all balls after each escape.
practice-one-rail-kick.progression: Aim for four target contacts in five as a suggested practice goal, then change the starting diamond.

setups.title: One-rail kick reference
setups.note: Target behind a blocker; a geometric cushion reference starts the escape comparison. Prepared aim is adjusted from the geometric reference for the default simulator cushion response; recalibrate on your table.

existingPractice.Goal: Build a reliable diamond reference before adding rails.
existingPractice.Setup: One blocker, one target object ball, and a clear one-rail route.
existingPractice.Measure: Make legal target contact on at least 4 of 5 attempts from each tested start.
existingPractice.Trainer: Use the kick tool, diamonds, and a saved layout to compare aim points.

practice-two-rail-kick.title: Two-rail kick extension
practice-two-rail-kick.purpose: Plan a multi-cushion route as a sequence of observable rail contacts.
practice-two-rail-kick.instruction: Name every cushion in order. Mark the first aim reference, predict the second/third crossing, and keep speed and spin fixed. Correct the earliest wrong contact first.
practice-two-rail-kick.success: Record the rail sequence, target contact, and legal outcome separately for five attempts. Do not infer a specific diamond-system formula from an unlabeled starter.
practice-two-rail-kick.transfer: Use the printed diagram and diamond references. For a named system such as Corner-5, use the linked creator lesson for its exact numbering and spin convention.
practice-two-rail-kick.progression: Test a second start only after the original route repeats; record each adjustment.

setups.title: Two-rail kick extension
setups.note: Two-cushion image route around the blocker; check each rail contact before the final target. Prepared aim is adjusted from the geometric reference for the default simulator cushion response; recalibrate on your table.

existingPractice.Goal: Extend a calibrated route to a second cushion.
existingPractice.Setup: Choose a repeatable two-rail route with no unintended ball contact.
existingPractice.Measure: Make legal target contact on at least 4 of 5 attempts before moving the starting point.
existingPractice.Trainer: Use diamond and half-diamond references and compare the two rail contact points.

practice-corner-five.title: Corner-5 three-rail route
practice-corner-five.purpose: Plan a multi-cushion route as a sequence of observable rail contacts.
practice-corner-five.instruction: Name every cushion in order. Mark the first aim reference, predict the second/third crossing, and keep speed and spin fixed. Correct the earliest wrong contact first.
practice-corner-five.success: Record the rail sequence, target contact, and legal outcome separately for five attempts. Do not infer a specific diamond-system formula from an unlabeled starter.
practice-corner-five.transfer: Use the printed diagram and diamond references. For a named system such as Corner-5, use the linked creator lesson for its exact numbering and spin convention.
practice-corner-five.progression: Test a second start only after the original route repeats; record each adjustment.

setups.title: Corner-5 three-rail route
setups.note: Two-cushion image route around the blocker; check each rail contact before the final target. Prepared aim is adjusted from the geometric reference for the default simulator cushion response; recalibrate on your table.

existingPractice.Goal: Use one consistent numbering system for a three-rail route.
existingPractice.Setup: Use the linked lesson for the Corner-5 numbering and reference route.
existingPractice.Measure: For this plan, make legal target contact on 4 of 5 selected escape attempts.
existingPractice.Trainer: Mark rail references on the Trainer; record the adjustment for each start.

main-shot-1-cue-tip-contact.progression: Use a smaller zone only after consistent pocketing and position; then increase approach distance.

main-shot-1-power-meter-c.transfer: Use the same shot and find the gentlest repeatable physical stroke that pockets the ball with a useful leave. Record pot and position separately.
main-shot-1-power-meter-c.progression: Compare a longer approach while keeping the target/pocket fixed.

drill-stop-shot.title: Stop Shot Calibration
drill-stop-shot.purpose: Arrive at a straight full-ball collision without forward or backward roll.
drill-stop-shot.instruction: Use a straight shot with no sidespin. Start slightly below center, keep aim fixed, and adjust one of tip height or speed. Observe the cue-ball center at impact and at rest.
drill-stop-shot.success: Keep the existing three-inch white target. Record the pot and cue-ball center inside the circle separately on five attempts. The circle is behind the object-ball center at the cue-ball impact position.
drill-stop-shot.transfer: Use the setup sheet and choose the same stopping tolerance on the cloth. Record pot and stop separately; recreate the original ball centers after every attempt.
drill-stop-shot.progression: Increase approach distance; regain the stop with speed and tip height rather than assuming center-tip contact always means stun.

drill-stun-tangent.title: 90-Degree Stun Tangent Line
drill-stun-tangent.purpose: Predict the initial cue-ball exit for a cut struck with stun at impact.
drill-stun-tangent.instruction: Keep sidespin at zero. Compare the tangent reference with the initial path after collision. Adjust tip height or speed to approach stun; then compare follow and draw.
drill-stun-tangent.success: Predict the initial exit side on three cuts, then record the pot and whether the initial route follows your tangent reference. Do not grade the entire follow/draw curve as a straight tangent.
drill-stun-tangent.transfer: Use the cut layout and identify a rail crossing along the tangent. Test five attempts; watch the initial exit separately from the eventual stopping point.
drill-stun-tangent.progression: Change cut angle, then compare how follow/draw move the route away from the reference.

drill-speed-ladder.title: Speed Ladder — Four Zones

drill-speed-ladder.instruction: Choose a clear path. Name a stopping band, then test low, medium, and higher speeds from the same start. Reset between attempts.
drill-speed-ladder.success: Use the four existing target zones in order. Record the cue-ball center inside/outside each named zone; reset to the original cue-ball start for every attempt.
drill-speed-ladder.transfer: Use a cue-ball-only route and flat target band. Translate stroke strength by observed travel; simulator speed values are not a measurement of your physical stroke.
drill-speed-ladder.progression: Narrow the band or add a cushion only after establishing a consistent baseline.

drill-wagon-wheel.purpose: Pocket the current ball while preserving a usable angle on the next ball.
drill-wagon-wheel.instruction: Name the next ball and pocket first. Mark a cue-ball zone and explain the angle it preserves. Execute Shot, inspect the actual simulated leave, and compare one speed or tip adjustment.
drill-wagon-wheel.success: Use the six existing colored targets one at a time. Record the pot and cue-ball center in the named target separately for each spoke; reset the starting balls between attempts.

drill-wagon-wheel.progression: Shrink the useful zone or add a third ball; do not count an attractive leave that is blocked.

drill-mirror-kick.title: One-Rail Mirror Kick
drill-mirror-kick.purpose: Reach the legal target through a cushion route when direct access is blocked.
drill-mirror-kick.instruction: Name the target and required rail sequence. Keep speed and sidespin consistent while adjusting only the first rail aim point. Check that the blocker is avoided.
drill-mirror-kick.success: Record target first-contact, scratch, and the game-required rail/pot condition on five attempts. A target touch is a contact score, not automatically a legal shot.
drill-mirror-kick.transfer: Copy the blocker and target. Identify the cushion-nose contact by diamond reference; reset all balls after each escape.
drill-mirror-kick.progression: Aim for four target contacts in five as a suggested practice goal, then change the starting diamond.

main-cue-shaft-preset.title: Cue / Shaft Preset
main-cue-shaft-preset.purpose: Use Cue / Shaft Preset correctly within the current lesson.
main-cue-shaft-preset.instruction: Cue and Shaft Preset is in Advanced Physics and Calibration. Standard shaft keeps the original squirt setting. Low-deflection shaft reduces squirt while keeping the same tip spin. Custom opens the cue ball to end-mass ratio for individual adjustment. The choice applies to both shots and is saved with your settings.
main-cue-shaft-preset.success: Predict the initial deflection side and identify the correction needed. Record contact accuracy for five physical trials, keeping the cue/shaft the same.
main-cue-shaft-preset.transfer: Recreate a long approach. Observe initial departure separately from later curvature; use your own cue response rather than assuming the preset matches it exactly.
main-cue-shaft-preset.progression: Compare distances before introducing elevation and swerve.

fundamentals-pre-shot-routine.title: A repeatable pre-shot routine
fundamentals-pre-shot-routine.purpose: Make planning and delivery a repeatable physical routine.
fundamentals-pre-shot-routine.instruction: While standing, choose pocket, route, and finish. Approach along the aim line, form a comfortable stance and bridge, rehearse smoothly, pause as needed, and deliver. Stand up and restart if the plan changes.
fundamentals-pre-shot-routine.success: Complete the same named sequence on five physical attempts. Record routine completed separately from potting; the simulator cannot observe your body or delivery.
fundamentals-pre-shot-routine.transfer: Use the straight-shot layout. Have a partner observe or record video, then review consistency of the routine rather than copying a prescribed body shape.
fundamentals-pre-shot-routine.progression: Keep the same routine when moving from straight shots to cuts.

fundamentals-balanced-stance.title: Comfortable stance and cue clearance
fundamentals-balanced-stance.purpose: Build comfortable balance and cue clearance while maintaining the chosen line.
fundamentals-balanced-stance.instruction: Plan while standing. Approach the shot, place your feet comfortably, and check that your body stays steady and the cue can move freely. Rise and realign if needed.
fundamentals-balanced-stance.success: Across five easy shots, record stable balance and unobstructed cue movement separately from potting. This is a physical checklist, not a simulator score.
fundamentals-balanced-stance.transfer: Recreate the straight shot and observe from side/front video or with a coach. Adapt stance to your body; no single foot position is required.
fundamentals-balanced-stance.progression: Test a second table position without losing balance or cue clearance.

setups.title: Comfortable stance and cue clearance
setups.note: Approach distance and contact geometry selected for Comfortable stance and cue clearance.

fundamentals-stable-bridge.title: A stable bridge
fundamentals-stable-bridge.purpose: Support a repeatable cue line with a stable bridge.
fundamentals-stable-bridge.instruction: Form a comfortable open or closed bridge on clear cloth. Rehearse slowly and check the hand remains still while the cue moves freely. Keep the bridge distance comfortable and consistent.
fundamentals-stable-bridge.success: Count five attempts with a stable bridge and smooth cue travel. Record hand movement separately from the shot result.
fundamentals-stable-bridge.transfer: Practice at the physical table with a coach, partner, or video. The on-screen cue does not model hand support or bridge stability.
fundamentals-stable-bridge.progression: Try a rail bridge only after the clear-cloth bridge is comfortable.

setups.title: A stable bridge
setups.note: Approach distance and contact geometry selected for A stable bridge.

fundamentals-grip-and-delivery.title: Relaxed grip and straight delivery
fundamentals-grip-and-delivery.purpose: Deliver the cue through the intended tip contact with a relaxed grip.
fundamentals-grip-and-delivery.instruction: Choose center contact on an easy straight shot. Rehearse smoothly without squeezing or steering, then deliver through the ball while keeping the bridge stable.
fundamentals-grip-and-delivery.success: Record five attempts for intended contact, relaxed delivery, and pot separately. Use observation or video; a simulated pot cannot validate a physical stroke.
fundamentals-grip-and-delivery.transfer: Use the straight-shot diagram and a striped practice ball if available to inspect unintended spin. Ask a coach to review persistent delivery errors.
fundamentals-grip-and-delivery.progression: Increase distance only after delivery stays repeatable.

setups.title: Relaxed grip and straight delivery
setups.note: Approach distance and contact geometry selected for Relaxed grip and straight delivery.

fundamentals-cue-access.title: Reach, rail bridges, and cue access
fundamentals-cue-access.purpose: Include physical cue access and reach when judging whether a route is practical.
fundamentals-cue-access.instruction: Compare a clear-cloth cue-ball start with a rail-adjacent start. Identify bridge support, cue clearance, reach, and elevation before choosing the stroke.
fundamentals-cue-access.success: Explain which stroke can actually be delivered from each position. A simulated clear path alone does not establish physical cue access.
fundamentals-cue-access.transfer: Inspect the actual cue approach and use a mechanical bridge when needed. Do not stretch into an unstable stroke; compare a simpler accessible route.
fundamentals-cue-access.progression: Add one nearby object ball and reassess cue clearance before planning position.

setups.title: Reach, rail bridges, and cue access
setups.note: Rail-adjacent cue ball makes bridge support and physical cue access the central observation.
